newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast light crudes firm late, buyers gone.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast light crudes firm late, buyers gone.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices firmed with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) late Wednesday while Alaskan differentials stayed in the doldrums on a dearth of buying, traders said.
Buyers said Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude was too expensive, but few opted to bring in foreign barrels because weak demand and ample supply have cut margins this quarter.
"(Alaska North Slope) crude is expensive relative to refining margins but it's not expensive compared to imports," a trader said.
Spot prices for regular unleaded gasoline Los Angeles have fallen 4.75 cents a gallon since October 7, about six to eight cents below other major cities.
Alaska North Slope's (ANS) diff stayed $2.30 a barrel under December cash WTI.
Buyers said they kept bids at a $2.50 discount, while producers held offers at $2.10.
Outright ANS prices rose with benchmark WTI to $20.30/$20.60 a barrel, 10 cents higher than Tuesday.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) showed on Tuesday that West Coast refiners saw large builds in crude oil stored at their facilities.
The region's supply grew by 3.6 million barrels last week, according to data from the API.
Line 63 ended 10 cents over Tuesday, with the range talked $19.50/19.80 a barrel.
Wilmington remained at $18.15/$18.25 a barrel, while Kern River crude stayed $16.65/$16.85 a barrel.
